clue.text: High and dry area reduced to dust

parts.note: ground means crushed or milled to powder

explanation.surface: A parched region has been pulverised into dust.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat stranded on the shore is left high and dry, an idiom for being stuck ashore.

clue.text: Adult beaten becomes embarrassed

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
bashed means struck or beaten

explanation.surface: A grown-up who has been beaten up feels humiliated.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashed is a synonym: feeling ashamed or self-conscious.

clue.text: Republican on about mother being Catholic

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word on wraps round the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A Republican politician talks about his mother's Catholic faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman is shorthand for Roman Catholic, the church of Rome.

clue.text: Row with subordinate causes stress

parts.note: under can mean lower in rank, subordinate
a line is a row, as of people or seats

explanation.surface: A quarrel with a junior employee leads to tension at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel and 'stress' as tension, but Row is a line and stress is the verb to emphasise.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline a point is to emphasise or stress it, from marking words with a line beneath.

clue.text: Pottery expert embracing student

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the student goes within the word for expert

parts.note: deft means skilful or expert
L stands for learner, a student driver in Britain

explanation.surface: A ceramics specialist takes a student under their wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white tin-glazed earthenware made in the Dutch town of that name.

clue.text: Baby carriage seen outside a Post Office

indicators.note: seen outside means placed around, so the carriage word goes round the rest

parts.note: carriage in the sense of posture or bearing, a pose

explanation.surface: A pram is spotted parked outside the post office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baby carriage' looks like one phrase meaning a pram; split it so 'Baby' is the definition and 'carriage' means bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Papoose is a word, from Algonquian, for a young Native American child, and so a baby.

clue.text: Screw fitting round well worker initially removed

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for fitting goes about what follows

parts.note: proper means fitting or suitable

indicators.note: removed signals taking away a letter from the word well

parts.note: taken as the word well before its first letter goes

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of worker

explanation.surface: Someone fits a screw around a well once the lead workman has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' looks like a verb going with 'fitting', but it is the noun for a ship's propeller; 'removed' leaves ELL once the worker's initial goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's screw is its propeller, the rotating blades that drive it.

clue.text: Polecat scent: it's ruined scientific study!

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A polecat's stink has wrecked a laboratory experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of it's stands for is, a link: only POLECAT SCENT IT is shuffled, and 'ruined' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plate tectonics is the branch of geology studying how the Earth's crustal plates move.

clue.text: Drive out farm vehicles capsized in Oise

indicators.note: in places the turned-over vehicles inside the river name

parts.note: taken as written: the Oise is a French river

indicators.note: capsized means turned over, so in a down clue the word is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: carts are farm vehicles

explanation.surface: Farm carts overturned in the River Oise must be cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oise is a river in northern France; 'capsized' suits a boat, and here makes STRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: To ostracise is to exclude or banish someone from a group, as the Athenians did by vote.

clue.text: Thrills lover no longer mentions

parts.note: an ex is a former lover
cites means mentions or quotes

explanation.surface: Hearing an old flame name-checked still gives someone a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: Excites is a synonym of thrills, both meaning stirs up strong feeling.

clue.text: Bananas found in messy lair — see creature

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside, so mad goes within the jumbled den
messy says the letters of lair are in disorder

parts.note: bananas is slang for mad
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: Bananas discovered in an untidy den: look at the animal responsible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' reads as fruit but is slang for mad; 'messy' gives ARIL, and 'see' is the archaic lo.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is a burrowing American mammal with a bony armoured shell, a creature.

clue.text: Ancient Mexican sleuth going after a Zulu

indicators.note: going after puts the sleuth word behind the other pieces

parts.note: Z is Zulu in the NATO phonetic alphabet
tec is short for detective, a sleuth

explanation.surface: A detective pursues a Zulu warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the people whose empire ruled central Mexico before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Biden's accolade for screen star Blackman?

definitions.meaning: an accolade or distinction, spelt the American way as President Biden would
... Blackman was the actress of The Avengers and Goldfinger

explanation.surface: Might the President present an award to a film actress?
explanation.walkthrough: Biden signals the American spelling without a U.
explanation.definitionFit: An honor is a distinction or award, and Honor was Blackman's first name.

clue.text: Halt event rearranged in old eastern region

indicators.note: rearranged means put in a different order, signalling these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A stopped event gets rescheduled somewhere in the old Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: The Levant was the historical name for the lands of the eastern Mediterranean, from the French for sunrise.

clue.text: Unusually deft clue I penned? Sneaky!

indicators.note: penned means shut in, so the I is enclosed by the jumbled letters
unusually means in an odd way, so these letters take an odd arrangement

explanation.surface: A setter boasts of having written an unusually clever clue, a sly one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges DEFT CLUE; 'penned' puts I inside. 'Penned' reads as written, but means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceitful means dishonest or underhand, behaving in a sneaky way.

clue.text: Extensive cover needed with account and IOUs

parts.note: a cap is a covering, such as a lid or hat

explanation.surface: Wide insurance cover is needed for an account full of debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacious means roomy, holding a great deal, so wide or extensive.

clue.text: Is it TV that's weird in whimsical celebration?

indicators.note: in places the jumble inside the word for whimsical

parts.note: fey means whimsical or otherworldly

indicators.note: weird means strange, so these letters are set in strange order

explanation.surface: A strange television show appears inside a fanciful party.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and capitals make IS IT TV look like a query about television; 'weird' shuffles it to STIVIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Festivity is a synonym for celebration or merrymaking.

clue.text: Composer Arthur finds perfect happiness

definitions.meaning: Sir Arthur ... was an English composer and Master of the Queen's Music

explanation.surface: A composer finds total contentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Bliss is complete joy, and also the surname of the English composer Arthur.

clue.text: Strike at revolutionary brave man in military unit

parts.note: bat means hit or strike

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word at is turned backwards

parts.note: a lion is a courageous person

explanation.surface: A rebel hero strikes out at the army battalion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a rebel describing the brave man, but it turns the preceding word back to TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is an army unit of several companies, part of a regiment.

clue.text: Gym in Parisian street making money

indicators.note: in puts the gym letters inside the French street

parts.note: rue is French for street
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: A gym on a Paris street is making a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India and other South Asian countries.

clue.text: Fierce competition in the rodent population?

definitions.meaning: the relentless struggle for success in work
a race in the sense of a breed of animals: here the rats

explanation.surface: Competition among rats is fierce.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is an idiom for the competitive grind of working life; read literally it is the race of rats.

clue.text: Drinks in luxurious hotel given poor press coverage?

indicators.note: coverage means covering, so the jumbled letters go round the hotel name
poor means badly done, so the word press is muddled

parts.note: the Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London

explanation.surface: Drinking at a posh hotel earns bad newspaper reviews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press coverage' reads as media reporting; 'poor' gives SPERS and 'coverage' wraps it round. The Ritz is a London luxury hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Spritzers are drinks of white wine mixed with soda water.

clue.text: Conceal empty suitcase on Greek island

indicators.note: empty means with the middle taken out, leaving only the outside letters of suitcase

parts.note: Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: Someone hides an empty suitcase on Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to hide it away, a synonym of conceal.

clue.text: See 6 Down
Entertainment round piano with English artist

parts.note: O is round in shape
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A show going round the piano, with an English painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is a form of staged musical drama, a kind of entertainment.

clue.text: American in boat cut fare from Japan

indicators.note: in puts the American letters inside the shortened boat
cut means trimmed, so the boat word loses its final letter

parts.note: a ship is a boat
US is short for American, the United States

explanation.surface: An American on a ship eats raw fish from Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is the Japanese dish of vinegared rice, often with raw fish, so food from Japan.

clue.text: Upstairs room that ticks boxes

indicators.note: boxes means holds inside, so the answer is contained in the words that ticks

explanation.surface: An upstairs room that meets every requirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ticks boxes' reads as the idiom for meeting requirements, but 'boxes' is the signal enclosing the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is a room just under the roof, at the top of the house.

clue.text: Signal for pick-me-up?

parts.note: a hitchhiker sticks out a digit to ask a passing driver for a lift, a pick-up; pick-me-up usually means a tonic

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick-me-up' looks like a tonic or drink, but read literally it is a request to be picked up by a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchhikers raise this digit to signal that they want a ride.

clue.text: Chap in Aberdare cleared out home

indicators.note: in puts the chap inside the remaining outside letters
cleared out means emptied, leaving only the first and last letters of Aberdare

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person, a chap

explanation.surface: A man in a Welsh town has cleared out his house.
explanation.walkthrough: Aberdare is a town in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a place where someone lives, a dwelling or home.

clue.text: Start research organisation?

definitions.meaning: a body for research or learning

explanation.surface: Launch a scientific body.
explanation.definitionFit: Institute is both a verb meaning initiate and a noun for an academic or research body.

clue.text: City visit involves son in great delight

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: involves means takes inside, so the visit word wraps round the son

parts.note: a stay is a visit

explanation.surface: A trip to the city with one's son brings joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is a state of overwhelming joy or rapture.

clue.text: Sappers leaving one French city for base

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: leaving means departing from, so the sappers are taken out of the city

parts.note: Grenoble is a city in the French Alps
RE, the Royal Engineers, are the British Army's sappers

explanation.surface: Army engineers swap one French city for a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military camp but means low and dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the sense of morally low; ignoble means dishonourable or mean.
